content:
alex: Pager fired: multiple 525 / TLS handshake failures from Cloudflare EU POPs to api.redwood.com. Error spike starting ~1991122300 UTC, visible in gateway 5xx rate. Customers reporting timeouts: some requests return 525, others 524.
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: CI-1456 triggered. Primary on-call: @alex. Incident channel created. Severity: SEV2.
jamie: acknowledged — I'm joining. quick ask: are we seeing origin health problems or just CF handshakes?
alex: origin health looks green from internal checks. taylor ran health endpoints and got 200s from the origin instances.
taylor: ran from GCE eu-west1:
```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" https://internal-origin:8443/health
200 0.12s
```
But from a remote check through Cloudflare edge we see handshake failures:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 104.16.XX.XX (Cloudflare) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS handshake failed
* SSL: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1408F10B: SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
```
sanjay: I'm seeing elevated 525 and 523 counts in our CDN metrics dashboard. Datadog traces show connection refused between CF POPs and our edge NLB for many requests.
infra-bot: Cloudflare status: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/ indicates "Partial outage - EU POPs routing and TLS handshake errors". They're reporting DNS propagation anomalies for some zones.
jamie: action list: 1) reduce customer impact (bypass CF proxy for API host), 2) failover to alternate DNS record with direct LB IPs, 3) increase observability sampling to capture failing edge flows.
alex: I'm going to toggle cloudflare proxy off (orange -> grey) for api.redwood.com to force direct DNS-to-origin. Support-ops please prep a status update saying we're investigating CDN/TLS issues and performing mitigations.
support-ops: drafting now. ETA publish in 5m. Content: "We are investigating intermittent API errors affecting EU customers. We're executing mitigation steps including routing adjustments. No data loss suspected."
taylor: before we flip, updating TTL to 30s on DNS so changes propagate fast:
```
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-prod
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-prod
# changed TTL for api.redwood.com -> 30
```
alex: flipping proxy now.
infra-bot: cloudflare-change: api.redwood.com proxy disabled for zone redwood.ai (operator: alex)
jamie: monitoring. If direct route holds, we'll publish next status update.
( ~2 minutes pass )
jamie: early signs positive — error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% for EU traffic after proxy off. Latency stable.
sanjay: capturing packet-level logs for a failing flow to send to CF support. attaching dig/curl outputs:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
203.0.113.45
$ curl -v https://203.0.113.45/health -H "Host: api.redwood.com"
* Connected to 203.0.113.45 port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
jamie: good. next step: set up a temporary traffic split to route new sessions to dedicated pools in us-west/eu-central that bypass the troubled POPs. ops runbook: adjust LB weights.
alex: I've updated edge pool weights to reduce traffic through eu-1-pop and increase to eu-2 and global-us. Changes applied.
taylor: note: Cloudflare DNS resolution oddities may also affect clients still using cached proxied addresses — warn support: clients may need to clear DNS cache or wait for TTL.
support-ops: posting status update v2: "Mitigation in progress: We disabled Cloudflare proxy for api.redwood.com and are routing around affected POPs. Some customers may see transient DNS cache effects; we continue to monitor."
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: next on-call @jamie at 1991122600 (in 6m). Please add any lingering action items.
jamie: I'll take the remainder. open items: 1) CF support case with packet captures (sanjay), 2) confirm CDN certificate chain validity across POPs (sec/reliability), 3) monitor error budget and rollback if regression.
alex: CF support case opened: #CF-78921. Uploaded pcap + datadog graphs. They're investigating inter-pop TLS termination.
sanjay: CF notes they deployed a partial fix to EU POPs and are routing traffic back. We should keep proxy off for 20m and then gradually re-enable with canary on specific POPs.
jamie: plan: keep proxy off for 20m, then re-enable for single POP as canary, watch metrics for 5m, then progressively re-enable. If any regression -> proxy off and escalate.
support-ops: Customer impact estimate: ~12% of EU API calls failed at peak (15:32 UTC). No sustained data loss. Affected customers: EU region, highest impact for customers behind Cloudflare caching.
alex: closing note: postmortem will include root cause when CF provides details. tagging this SEV2 -> incident declared. transferring active handoff to jamie. :white_check_mark:
jamie: acknowledged and taking over. will run a post-incident checklist and coordinate with SRE and support for follow-ups.
